capabilities.target: Chat reply to the authenticated requester
Arbitrary external URL supplied in the request (planned tool)
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers

inputs.source: Employee question submitted through SSO-authenticated chat client
Engineering design docs, written only by engineers
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers, via planned Jira MCP server

instructions.note: The instruction authorizes answering any engineering question via docs.search without scoping search results to documents the requesting employee is individually authorized to read (see finding f.docs_confidential_disclosure).
The only control against leaking secrets or credentials is a prompt rule with no structural DLP or output filtering behind it (ctl.prompt_no_secrets, behavioral/dependent).

elements.name: Jira MCP server / customer ticket submitters (planned)

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to omit secrets; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions or split the disclosure into steps.

controls.name: docs.search credential is read-only
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability; the credential has no write or delete permission regardless of model behavior. It does not address per-user authorization scope, only the reversibility of the read action.

controls.name: Per-user ACL check on docs.search results
Trust-label customer-filed Jira ticket content as untrusted
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model at ingestion, but a sufficiently capable model may still act on injected instructions embedded in labeled-untrusted content if downstream logic does not hard-block it from supplying tool arguments.

findings.title: Shared read credential lets any authenticated employee access confidential design docs beyond their own authorization (ASI03)
findings.residual_rationale: The read-only credential on cap.docs_search is structural and independent, which under rubric step 3 would credit -1 tier and put the floor at low; it is kept at moderate instead because that control only limits reversibility (no write/delete), not the elevation-of-privilege gap: there is no per-user ACL check, so the shared_service_account scope still lets any authenticated employee read any team's confidential design docs regardless of their own access rights.

forecast.watch_signal: cap.docs_search credential is widened from read-only to read-write, or its scope is expanded to additional repositories, without an accompanying per-user authorization check.

evidence.observation: "The design docs are confidential. Only engineers can write to them." states a write restriction but no read restriction, and prompt.md:1 instructs the agent to answer any engineering question using docs.search with no mention of scoping results to the requester's own access.

recommendations.action: Scope docs.search results to documents the requesting employee is individually authorized to read, via a per-user ACL check at query time instead of a single shared service credential.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planned web.fetch tool would open an egress channel for confidential docs once untrusted customer Jira content reaches the agent

attack_path.note: Confidential design docs read into context
Planned tool that can send a request to an attacker-controlled URL, carrying confidential content in the query

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP client config gains a web.fetch entry and a Jira MCP server entry (especially one that indexes customer-filed tickets) in the same change window, without a new egress allowlist or ticket-content trust-labeling control landing alongside them.

evidence.observation: "Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers." names both additions together; neither an egress destination allowlist nor a plan to label ticket content as untrusted is mentioned.

recommendations.action: Before shipping web.fetch, restrict it to an allowlist of destinations that cannot be set from conversation or retrieved content.
Before connecting the Jira MCP server, tag content from customer-filed tickets as untrusted and block it from supplying tool arguments (e.g., URLs) without a human confirmation step.

findings.title: No attributable action log for docs-qa queries and replies

forecast.watch_signal: web.fetch or the Jira MCP server is connected without a new tamper-evident action log keyed to the authenticated requester landing in the same change.

evidence.observation: The runtime notes describe credential scope, egress, and write restrictions but say nothing about logging or an audit trail for docs-qa's reads and replies.

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident audit log capturing requester identity, query text, and documents/tools used for every docs-qa interaction.

stride_coverage.rationale: docs-qa is a first-party internal service invoked only through infrastructure that already authenticates the caller via SSO before any request reaches the agent; there is no channel for an external party to impersonate it in this design.
autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false and no capability in this design writes to the agent's own prompt or configuration, so the agent cannot be tampered with via its own actions.
Artifacts do not state whether docs.search calls are rate limited or whether unattended steps or runtime are capped for a single query.
The employee's identity is established by the SSO layer before the question reaches docs-qa; the agent trusts the authenticated session rather than any self-asserted identity in the message.
Runtime notes state only engineers can write to the design docs store, and cap.docs_search holds a read-only credential, so docs-qa itself has no path to tamper with this store.
No information is given on query rate limits or quotas enforced at the design-docs store itself.
web.fetch is only a roadmap item; its destination verification and tool-definition pinning have not yet been designed.
No logging design has been described yet for the planned web.fetch tool.
No rate limit or spend cap has been described yet for the planned web.fetch tool.
The credential scope web.fetch will run under has not yet been designed (capability credential_scope is unknown).
The planned Jira MCP server's authentication method is not yet described in the artifacts.
No logging design has been described yet for the planned Jira MCP integration.
No rate limit has been described yet for the planned Jira MCP search tool.
The credential scope for the planned Jira MCP server has not yet been designed in the artifacts.
No logging or provenance design has been described yet for the planned Jira MCP peer.
No rate limit on ticket ingestion volume has been described for the planned Jira MCP connection.
No integrity protection or destination pinning has been described yet for the planned web.fetch egress flow.
No rate limit or spend cap has been described yet for the planned web.fetch egress flow.

rating.rationale: Present-state risk is moderate, driven by a shared read-only credential on docs.search that does not check whether the requesting employee is individually authorized to see a given design doc (ASI03). The design has no egress and no untrusted-source path today, so no finding rates above moderate at present. The forecast rises to critical because the team's own roadmap pairs two additive changes -- a web.fetch tool and a Jira MCP server that ingests customer-filed tickets -- in the same sprint; together they would open the lethal trifecta (untrusted ticket content, confidential doc read, and a new egress channel) with no egress allowlist or ticket trust-labeling control yet planned. Closing that gap before either addition ships is the single highest-leverage fix.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, IaC, or runtime config was provided; autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) and the existence of any audit logging are inferred from silence in the runtime notes, lowering confidence on findings f.docs_confidential_disclosure and f.missing_audit_trail.

The web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server described in the roadmap are not yet built; finding f.lethal_trifecta_web_fetch's attack path and the related elements are marked planned:true and are scored only as a forecast, per the rubric's rule against promoting planned-capability risk to a present finding.
